evaluations.label: A
errors: Action item assigns Andrei to 'Follow up with absent team members (Maggie, Pierrette)'; in the transcript Susan volunteered to ask Maggie and Pierrette
Action item 'Distribute documents of the new office configuration' was done during the meeting, not a follow-up task
Summary says preferences will be collected and proposals merged with the other group 'before next Tuesday's review meeting'; merging with the other group comes after the proposals, not before Tuesday

'Management recognizes this [lounge] as a priority due to previously lengthy discussions on its value' is not supported; the lounge's role was explicitly left open and Susan questioned the need for it
'Lounge Priority: A lounge/reading room is key...' overstates agreement; it was debated and left undecided
'desk arrangements inside rooms can be flexible' misstates the point: what is open is which people go in which rooms
'The session will focus on refining the plan rather than final decisions' (next meeting) is invented
'Project grouping seen as less important than proximity to meeting rooms and shared spaces' is a garbled reading of the discussion
Several timestamps are wrong (e.g. office details at 00:06, project grouping at 18:14)
strengths: Very broad coverage: numbers (15 people, 18 positions, 16 with reading room), equipment, smoking, coffee, Gisela, room splitting, 4 desks in 3P room
Captures the other group's parallel proposal and that today was about constraints only
Lists most of the investigation items Andre took on
weaknesses: Very long and repetitive; the same points (no growth, room splitting hurdles) repeat across several sections
Wrong owner on the Maggie/Pierrette action and a non-action listed as an action
Some invented or overstated claims about the lounge and next meeting

evaluations.label: B
errors: 'Majority lean toward a mixed-use room' overstates it; Martin said some people want a mixed room and that no decision had been taken
'Strong support for a dedicated lounge/reading room' glosses over Susan asking whether it was needed
Option of giving Gisela 'a 2P room with a visitor slot' is listed without noting the group found a visitor in the admin office unrealistic except for students or interns
strengths: Concise, well organized and easy to scan
Key numbers correct (15 people, ~18 positions, 16 with a 2P reading room, zero growth)
Next steps cover all the open investigations: room separation, 4 desks in 3P room, Gisela with school admin, Maggie and Pierrette, each attendee's sketch, Tuesday around 2 PM after the MDM meeting
Correct attributions for Susan's and Martin's positions
weaknesses: Next steps have no owners (e.g. Susan for Maggie and Pierrette, Andre for the investigations)

evaluations.label: C
errors: 'Action Items: (none)' although several were assigned (Andre to check room separation, Susan to ask Maggie and Pierrette, everyone to bring a proposal)

Says professor sharing with assistants is 'common in other faculties but not necessarily here'; the transcript says the reverse: it is the school's tradition, while other faculties give professors their own offices
'accommodate approximately 15 to 18 people' muddles 15 people with 18 positions
'Members were tasked with consulting colleagues, such as Maggie and Pierrette' - Susan specifically volunteered for that
'negotiation with other groups in the building' misstates the single other group working on the same space
Uses 'Speaker 1/2/3/4' labels that do not match the transcript's speaker letters, making attributions unverifiable
strengths: Correctly lists the open questions (partitions, 4 in a 3P room, lounge role)
Mentions equipment placement and the Tuesday 2:00 PM follow-up
weaknesses: Speaker numbering is confusing and names are mostly absent
Misses decisions such as rejecting project grouping, the 16-slot and zero-growth arithmetic, and the smoking point

evaluations.label: D
errors: 'Susan and Martin both raised concerns about sharing offices' slightly overstates Martin, who said he had nothing against sharing (the sub-bullet corrects this)
strengths: Most accurate attributions: Martin on zero growth, meeting rooms for projects, the lounge being undecided, speaking only for oneself; Susan on confidential rectorate work and visitors
Clearly states what is fixed (room count) versus open (assignments) and that nothing was decided
Action items carry owners, including Susan for Maggie and Pierrette
weaknesses: Omits Andre's checks on fitting 4 desks in a 3P room and on placing Gisela with the school's other admin
'Everyone brings a sketch' is in the body but not in the action items
Leaves out coffee and cafeteria details and the reason for the afternoon time (MDM meeting)

rationale: B and D are both accurate and readable. B wins narrowly because its next steps cover every open investigation and the meeting logistics, though without owners. D has the most precise attributions and correct owners but leaves out two of Andre's follow-ups. A covers a lot but is bloated and contains real errors, including the wrong owner for the Maggie/Pierrette action and invented claims about the lounge. C lists no action items, reverses the point about other faculties, and uses speaker numbers that cannot be mapped.
